title: Robin Wood - Klimapolitik im Strudel der Desinformation (Serie 998: CX - Corax - Umwelt - Grünes)
description: Die Gruppe Robin Wood arbeitet seit vielen Jahren zum Thema Klimaschutz, Klimagerechtigkeit, Klimawandel und allem, was da irgendwie so dranhängt. Die Themenbandbreite, welche sie vom ursprünglichen Einsatz für die Wälder in Deutschland inzwischen entwickelt haben, ist riesig. Von Protesten gegen Autobahnausbauten bis hin zum Thema Privatjets. Auch öffentlicher Nahverkehr statt Panzerproduktion ist in den letzten Jahren ein Schwerpunkt geworden, aber auch so grundlegende Sachen wie Lieferketten und Ökostrom. Dabei setzt die Gruppe auch auf spektakuläre Aktionen, zuletzt mit einem großen Banner an der Bundeszentrale der CDU. Doch ihre Aktionen sind nicht nur auf Deutschland beschränkt, so beschäftigen sie sich zum Beispiel auch mit der finnischen Forstwirtschaft. Über die Jahre hat sich dementsprechend bei Robin Wood viel Erfahrung angesammelt, wie Öffentlichkeitsarbeit rund um das Thema Klimagerechtigkeit erfolgreich funktionieren kann – doch auch Robin Wood kämpft mit einer Zunahme an Desinformation in der digitalen Öffentlichkeit. Radio CORAX sprach über die Auswirkungen von Desinformation und die Konsequenzen, Tipps für gute Berichterstattung über Klimathemen und auch ihre Perspektive auf die anstehende Klimakonferenz in Antalya, die COP31 mit Ute Bertrand. Sie ist Pressesprecherin von Robin Wood, seit über 30 Jahren in der Umweltbewegung aktiv und sitzt im Landesrundfunkrat des NDR. Dieses Gespräch entstand im Rahmen des Projekts "Sonic Resilience" (Link: https://radiocorax.de/tag/sonicresilience/)

title: Sozialstaat zu teuer? Vielleicht ist nur der Reichtum zu billig.
description: Es geht um Sozialabbau, Pflege, Befristungen, die wachsende Schere zwischen Arm und Reich – und um die Frage, warum so oft über Rentner, Grundsicherung und „faule“ Beschäftigte gestritten wird, aber viel seltener über Vermögen, Erbschaften und Verteilung. title: An Inhuman Future: Nick Land, Techno-Accelerationism, and the Dark Enlightenment
description: In this episode Alyson and Breht enter the strange and unsettling world of Nick Land: Marx, Nietzsche, Delueze, cybernetics, accelerationism, and the possibility that capitalism is becoming something more than a human social system. For Land, techno-capital may be an inhuman process using humanity as a temporary vehicle - accelerating through markets, machines, computation, and artificial intelligence toward a future in which we are no longer necessary. We trace this vision from Land's anti-humanism and theory of deterritorialization to the Dark Enlightenment and neo-reaction, asking whether his philosophy is best understood as a kind of inverted Marxism: not humanity escaping capital, but capital escaping humanity. In the process, we discuss consciousness, artificial intelligence, historical and dialectical materialism, Land's influence on the techno-oligarchs, philosophy, and much more. After explaining and exploring Land's philosophy and politics, Alyson and Breht dismantle it via a Marxist Critique. Check out our episodes on: Julius Evola Louis Althusser Nietzsche ---------------------- Learn More about Rev Left and Red Menace HERE

title: Aggiornamenti dopo l'assemblea del 30\09 - Mobilitazione per la Palestina
description: Ascolta Durata 17m 36s Mobilitazione del 10 Ottobre - Restituzione assemblea del 30 Settembre con le parole di una compagna dei giovani palestinesi, oggi 1 Ottobre usciranno le informazioni sul corteo romano; il punto di ritrovo sarà al Colosseo per giungere poi in Piazzale Aldo Moro. Di seguito, riportiamo l'appello: Dopo tre anni di genocidio a Gaza, il popolo palestinese continua ad affrontare massacri, assedio, carestia e pulizia etnica, mentre in Cisgiordania si intensificano i raid militari e le violenze dei coloni. Nonostante il calo dell'attenzione mediatica e le false pacificazioni, i crimini e l'oppressione non si sono fermati. Il nostro dovere è riportare la centralità della lotta palestinese al centro del movimento politico e popolare in Italia. La causa palestinese non può essere liquidata come mera emergenza umanitaria, è una lotta politica per la liberazione. Il 10 ottobre scendiamo in piazza in tutte le città italiane per la fine immediata del genocidio, lo sblocco degli aiuti e il ritiro dell'esercito di occupazione. Saremo in piazza al fianco di tutti i popoli della regione che resistono all'imperialismo e alle aggressioni sioniste - in Yemen, Libano, Siria, Iraq e Iran - e contro le politiche di guerra che devastano i territori e le popolazioni. Esprimiamo inoltre piena solidarietà a chi, anche in Italia, subisce la repressione per essersi mobilitato al fianco del popolo palestinese e contro il genocidio. LE NOSTRE ISTANZE: * Stop alla guerra e all'economia di guerra: Blocco immediato del riarmo, contro l'aumento della spesa militare e l'invio, vendita e transito di armi da e verso l'entità sionista. Rescissione di ogni accordo di cooperazione militare, economica e accademica. * Stop alla criminalizzazione del dissenso: Ritiro immediato del "DDL Antisemitismo" (che usa la definizione IHRA per equiparare l'antisionismo all'antisemitismo e silenziare la critica politica) e contro i cosiddetti Decreti "Sicurezza" e tutte le misure repressive contro il movimento di solidarietà. * Libertà per i prigionieri politici in Italia: Liberazione immediata per Anan Yaeesh, Ahmed Salem, Mohammed Hannoun, Yaser Elasaly, Riyad Albustanji, Ra’ed Dawoud e Abdelnuti Abunada. * Per il diritto del popolo palestinese alla resistenza, in tutte le sue forme, per l'ottenimento del proprio legittimo diritto all'autodeterminazione, alla liberazione e al ritorno, in tutta la Palestina, dal fiume al mare. * Contro la complicità diretta dello Stato italiano, terzo esportatore al mondo di armi verso "Israele" e corresponsabile nel genocidio del popolo palestinese: chiediamo l'immediata cessazione di ogni accordo militare, economico, diplomatico e accademico con l’entità sionista, l'imposizione di sanzioni severe e un embargo totale sulle armi. * Contro le politiche di riarmo europeo e italiano che pretendono di destinare fino al 5% del PIL alle spese militari e all’industria bellica, a scapito dei diritti sociali, sottraendo risorse fondamentali a sanità, istruzione, lavoro e welfare. VERSO UNA MOBILITAZIONE POPOLARE E DEI LAVORATORI Invitiamo le comunità, i sindacati, le organizzazioni politiche, i collettivi e le strutture studentesche e dei lavoratori a mobilitarsi per costruire un embargo popolare e pratiche concrete di boicottaggio economico, accademico e militare, intrecciando la lotta contro il genocidio e la guerra con quella contro lo sfruttamento e l'attacco continuo a diritti sociali. 10 OTTOBRE 2026 Da Roma a Milano, da Napoli a Torino, da Bologna a Palermo e in tutte le piazze italiane: Partecipate alle manifestazioni. Alziamo la bandiera della Palestina.

title: Slow and Low 30.09.2026
Infomagazin 30.09.2026
[radio africa] Radio Africa: Etiopia, Marocco, Sudafrica
description: Ascolta Durata 48m 51s Etiopia : a quasi quattro anni dalla firma di un fragile accordo di pace a Pretoria nel novembre 2022, la guerra è tornata nel nord dell'Etiopia. La nuova coalizione all'offensiva in Tigray, Afar e Amhara è il risultato di un'inaspettata riconfigurazione delle alleanze tra gruppi armati che si sono scontrati in passato. Tutti condividono un unico nemico: il Primo Ministro Abiy Ahmed, contro il quale promettono una "guerra totale". La ripresa dei combattimenti sta già suscitando i peggiori timori. Con oltre 600.000 vittime, il precedente conflitto tra il braccio armato del Fronte di Liberazione del Popolo del Tigray (TPLF) e le Forze di Difesa Nazionali Etiopi (ENDF) è stato considerato uno dei conflitti più sanguinosi dell'inizio del XXI secolo. Ex nemici, i gruppi armati ora alleati sembrano intenzionati a seguire le orme della coalizione formata dal TPLF, che rovesciò l'ex dittatore Mengistu Haile Mariam, nel 1991. Il comunicato che annuncia la formazione dell'Alleanza delle Forze Popolari Etiopi per la Sopravvivenza descrive il governo di Abiy Ahmed come un "regime personalista, dittatoriale e genocida". La ripresa dei combattimenti s’inserisce in un quadro regionale estremamente complesso, che rischia di far esplodere la regione del Corno d’Africa. Marocco : il Marocco si sta risvegliando in un panorama politico in fermento, dopo le elezioni legislative del 23 settembre caratterizzate da un'affluenza alle urne ai minimi storici. La partecipazione ha superato di poco il 38%; bisogna risalire al 2007 per trovare una cifra inferiore. Il voto ha confermato la crisi di fiducia che affligge da anni il rapporto tra i marocchini e la classe politica. A causa della mancata risposta della classe politica ai problemi sociali che affliggono la popolazione marocchina come disoccupazione, perdita del potere d'acquisto, servizi pubblici insufficienti, molti elettori sono rimasti a casa. Questo drastico calo ha favorito il Partito Autenticità e Modernità (PAM), legato alla monarchia ma anche, e soprattutto, il Partito Giustizia e Sviluppo (PJD). Il partito islamista, spazzato via alle elezioni parlamentari del 2021, dove era sceso a 13 seggi, ha visto quadruplicare la propria rappresentanza. Ma i problemi del Marocco, dalla disoccupazione giovanile alle disparità dello sviluppo rimangono irrisolti. Sudafrica : i migranti africani in Sudafrica temono nuove proteste e possibili violenze alla scadenza del 30 settembre, fissata dal movimento anti-immigrazione March and March per chiedere agli stranieri senza documenti di lasciare il Paese. L’ultimatum ha accresciuto la preoccupazione soprattutto a Durban, dove nelle ultime settimane si sono già verificati scontri tra attivisti del movimento, rifugiati e richiedenti asilo. L’ostilità nei confronti degli stranieri starebbe colpendo anche persone regolarmente presenti nel Paese. Il movimento March and March ha organizzato proteste ben coordinate in tutto il paese. I suoi leader provengono dal KwaZulu-Natal, la roccaforte politica di Zuma, l’ex presidente. In Sudafrica, una serie orribile di femminicidi ha sconvolto la regione di Johannesburg. In soli tre mesi, otto donne sono state trovate morte, in un raggio di poche decine di chilometri. Questa ondata di omicidi ha suscitato indignazione e numerose richieste di intervento, soprattutto perché la lotta contro la violenza di genere è stata dichiarata una priorità nazionale dal presidente sudafricano.

title: Fermiamo il DDL Bavaglio
description: Ascolta Durata 13m 39s Con Tina, di Amnesty International, continuiamo a parlare dell'opposizione al "DDL Antisemitismo" e delle numerose mobilitazioni che si stanno organizzando in tutta Italia, da Milano a Catania, contro questa legge, che metterebbe un bavaglio alla denuncia delle politiche di Israele, finalizzate al genocidio della popolazione palestinese. Si tratta di una serie di azioni, movimenti e iniziative di tipo diverso, in preparazione della giornata di mobilitazione internazionale del 10 ottobre. E' possibile conoscere tutte le piazze italiane che sono attive da venerdì 2 ottobre sino a domenica 4 ottobre qui e qui . In conclusione, lanciamo l'appuntamento per il presidio di venerdì prossimo, 2 ottobre, dalle 14:00 alle 16:00, davanti a Montecitorio, in occasione della discussione del DDL Bavaglio in Aula, alla Camera. L'appuntamento è stato promosso da oltre 300 realtà che hanno sottoscritto l'appello per fermare la norma che, sovrapponendo la definizione di antisemitismo con il diritto di critica nei confronti delle politiche dello Stato di Israele, rischia di compromettere la libertà di opinione e il diritto al dissenso, sanciti dall'articolo 21 della nostra Costituzione.

title: An Inhuman Future: Nick Land, Techno-Accelerationism, and the Dark Enlightenment
description: In this episode Alyson and Breht enter the strange and unsettling world of Nick Land: Marx, Nietzsche, Delueze, cybernetics, accelerationism, and the possibility that capitalism is becoming something more than a human social system. For Land, techno-capital may be an inhuman process using humanity as a temporary vehicle - accelerating through markets, machines, computation, and artificial intelligence toward a future in which we are no longer necessary. We trace this vision from Land's anti-humanism and theory of deterritorialization to the Dark Enlightenment and neo-reaction, asking whether his philosophy is best understood as a kind of inverted Marxism: not humanity escaping capital, but capital escaping humanity. In the process, we discuss consciousness, artificial intelligence, historical and dialectical materialism, Land's influence on the techno-oligarchs, philosophy, and much more. After explaining and exploring Land's philosophy and politics, Alyson and Breht dismantle it via a Marxist Critique. Check out our episodes on: Julius Evola Louis Althusser Nietzsche ---------------------- Learn More about Rev Left and Red Menace HERE

description: Nicht nur seitens der AfD stehen Rundfunkmedien unter Beschuss, allen voran öffentlich-rechtliche Sender und freie Radios. Im FSK-Morgenmagazin haben wir mit dem Journalisten und ehemaligen Gewerkschaftsfunktionär bei ver.di, Martin Dieckmann, über gängige Missverständnisse gesprochen. Außerdem sprachen wir darüber, wie verschiedene Medien von der Verfassung geschützt sind und an welchen Stellen es Möglichkeiten der Mitgestaltung gibt.

title: “Sich nicht an den Zustand gewöhnen” – Demonstration zum Tag der Wohnungslosen in Hamburg (Serie 1445: FSK-Morgenmagazin)
description: Am 11. September war Tag der Wohnungslosen. Zu diesem Anlass rief das Bündnis “Solidarität statt Ausgrenzung” zur Demonstration auf. Der Beitrag verbindet Auszüge aus Redebeiträgen mit Interviewpassagen und ergänzenden Erklärungen, um die Situation in Hamburg zu beleuchten. Obwohl die Stadt das abstrakte Ziel formuliert hat, Obdachlosigkeit bis zum Jahr 2030 abzuschaffen, zielen konkrete Maßnahmen auf Verdrängung ab. Seit November 2025 verbindet die “Koordinierungsstelle für ausländische Straftäter und besonders auffällige Ordnungsstörer” (KOSTARS) etablierte ordnungspolitische Praktiken zudem mit Abschiebepolitik. Gleichzeitig wurden der aufsuchenden Sozialarbeit in Hamburg Mitte sämtliche Mittel gekürzt. Aber es gibt Handlungsmöglichkeiten: Im Oktober 2026 wird das Bündnis eine Petition übergeben, die u.a. die Ratifizierung des Rechts auf Wohnen und eine flächendeckende Housing-First-Politik fordert.

title: Peace Brigades International über ihre Arbeit in Mexiko und “shrinking spaces” in Deutschland (Serie 1445: FSK-Morgenmagazin)
description: Ein Erfahrungsaustausch über internationale Solidarität, gewaltfreie Schutzbegleitung und Freiwilligenarbeit an der Seite von bedrohten Menschenrechtsverteidiger:innen in Mexiko. Seit bald 30 Jahren steht Peace Brigades International in Mexiko an der Seite von Aktivist:innen, die aufgrund ihres Einsatz für Menschenrechte, Klimagerechtigkeit und indigene Gemeinden mit großen Gefahren konfrontiert sind. Doch zivilgesellschaftliche Handlungsräume (shrikinig spaces) für NGOs und soziale Bewegungen verengen sich aufgrund von Repressionen nicht nur in Mexiko, auch in Deutschland kommt es zunehmend zu Beschränkungen von Aktivismus und Engagement. Der ehemalige PBI-Mexiko Freiwillige Jonas berichtet im Gespräch mit Jakob über seine praktischen Erfahrungen aus der internationalen Menschenrechtsbegleitung: von Protestaktionen gegen gewaltsames Verschwindenlassen, die Dominanz des organisierten Verbrechens in Mexiko, menschenrechtlichen Risiko- und Sicherheitsanalysen und emotionaler Fürsorge in gewaltsamen Verhältnissen.

title: Antifa heißt: Gegen jeden Antisemitismus! Demo am 10. Oktober 2026 in Leipzig
description: ’Gegen jeden Antisemitismus – ob er sich völkisch gibt oder staatstragend, ob als „Israelkritik“ getarnt oder als „Widerstand“ verklärt. Gegen die, die ihn schüren und gegen die, die ihn beschweigen.’ So heißt es im Aufruf zur Demonstration "Antifa heißt: Gegen jeden Antisemitismus!", die am 10.10.26 in Leipzig stattfinden soll. Aufgerufen hat ein Bündnis verschiedener Leipziger Gruppen (werden im Beitrag benannt), die in der Woche der Jahrestage des Pogroms vom 7.10.23 in Israel und dem Anschlag des 9.10.19 in Halle, auf den immer weiter grassierenden Antisemitismus aufmerksam machen und ihn bekämpfen wollen. Wir sprachen mit einem Vertreter des Bündnisses über die Situation in Leipzig, den geplanten Ablauf und die Motivation hinter der Demo. title: Free All Antifas: appello conferma condanne ed estradizione
description: lettura delle sentenze di Maja, Anna e Gabriele Durata 15m , collegamento col presidio di Parigi Durata 10m 42s Aggiornamenti dalle sentenze della corte di appello per i "fatti di Budapest": ovvero sulla repressione della manifestazione antifascista in occasione del cosiddetto "Giorno dell'onore" ungherese, nota ricorrenza di celebrazione del nazifascismo. Confermate le condanne di Maja, Gabriele e Anna, con minime riduzioni delle pene rispetto alle sentenze precedenti: 7 anni, 6 anni, e sospensione della pena carceraria, rispettivamente. Confermata l'estradizione verso la Germania da parte della Francia per Gino (Rexhino Abazaj, di origine albanese). Ne parliamo in collegamento con compagni anche da Parigi, dove una diretta radiofonica è in onda dalle 10 del mattino alle 20 circa, presso la Bourse du Travail. Incontro pubblico alle 17:30 in solidarietà con Gino e contro la criminalizzazione dell'antifascismo. Come ci ricordano i compagni, lottare è ancora più difficile per chi non ha la cittadinanza giusta, allora continuiamo a mobilitarci anche per la partecipazione alle lotte e alla vita politica dei territori che abitiamo sans papiers .

title: Oggi assemblea verso il 10 ottobre - Palestina
description: Ascolta Durata 13m 28s E' prevista una assemblea cittadina verso la mobilitazione nazionale del 10 ottobre alle ore 17.00 presso l'Università di Roma La Sapienza, a Lettere in aula VI. per la fine del genocidio e la fine del sionismo. Qui il rapporto sulle complicità militari italiane nel genocidio in corso: https://www.embargoforpalestine.com/italia E il comunicato dell'assemblea: Facciamo appello a tutta la cittadinanza, alle organizzazioni e alle realtà antisioniste di Roma ad unirsi per un 10 ottobre schierati dalla parte di chi resiste. Saremo in piazza per sostenere il nostro popolo e il nostro movimento di liberazione, per onorare gli oltre settantatremila martiri di Gaza e i suoi combattenti, che da 78 anni resistono all'aggressione sionista, anche dopo la farsa del cosiddetto "cessate il fuoco" dell'ottobre 2025 e la finta pace, che ha spento i riflettori ma non ha fermato per un solo giorno i bombardamenti, le uccisioni e l'assedio. Saremo in piazza per tutta la Palestina, che da oltre un secolo si oppone all'occupazione e al progetto coloniale sionista, e per tutti i popoli che resistono all'imperialismo e al sionismo. Il governo italiano ha scelto chiaramente da che parte stare, sottraendo risorse al welfare nazionale per consegnarle all'industria della morte e colpendo con la repressione chiunque osi sfidarne la complicità con l'entità sionista. Il 10 ottobre tutte le città d'Italia, e anche noi qui da Roma, si mobiliteranno per ribadire che il nostro impegno non si fermerà finché non saranno conquistati la piena liberazione e il diritto al ritorno. VERSO IL CORTEO DEL 10 OTTOBRE ORA E SEMPRE RESISTENZA!

title: In Budapest und Paris wird gegen Antifaschist*innen verhandelt; die Strafe von Maja T. wurde leicht reduziert
Repression gegen Antifas im Budapest-Komplex - In Budapest und Paris wird gegen Antifaschist*innen verhandelt; die Strafe von Maja T. wurde leicht reduziert
description: Am heutigen Mittwoch stehen wichtige Gerichtsentscheidung im sogenannten Budapest-Komplex an. Verschiedenen Antifaschist*innen werden Angriffe auf Nazis beim sogenannten "Tag der Ehre" in Budapest vorgeworfen. Prominenteste angeklagte Person ist Maja T. Die nicht-binäre Antifaschist*in war verfassungswidrig von Deutschland nach Ungarn abgeschoben worden und war dort lange im Hungerstreik. Im Berufungsverfahren in Budapest wurde über Maja T., den Italiener Gabriele M. und Anna M.aus Berlin geurteilt. Majas Strafe wurde von 8 auf 7 Jahre reduziert. Zudem entscheidet heute, ebenfalls im Budapest-Komplex das Kassationsgericht in Paris darüber, ob der in Albanien geborene Antifaschist Gino nach Deutschland und von hier aus vielleicht später möglicherweise doch noch an die ungarische Justiz ausgeliefert werden kann. Wir haben mit unserem freien Mitarbeiter Luc in Paris gesprochen, der an einem Ticker fürs ND zu den Gerichtsentscheidungen beteiligt ist.

title: »Haltung zeigen« am Hr. Fleischer Kiosk - Mitmach-Performance zu Tierwohl & industrielle Haltungsformen (Serie 1513: CX - Corax - Lokales - Mikro)
description: Wenn man Fleisch kauft, gibt es ja neuerdings häufig dieses Label zur Haltungsform auf der Verpackung. Je besser die Haltungsform, desto höher das Tierwohl. Aber was bedeutet „Tierwohl“ beim Einkauf von Fleisch eigentlich? Im September und Oktober widmet sich Christin Philipp am Hr. Fleischer Kiosk in Halle den verschiedenen Haltungsformen von sog. „Nutztieren“. Er fragt danach, was sich hinter den Kennzeichnungen auf den Verpackungen verbirgt. Die Ausstellung will zeigen, was die Entscheidung an der Fleischtheke für die Tiere bedeutet. Ergänzt wird die Ausstellung durch performative Mitmach-Aktionen: Besucher*innen können selbst erfahren, was räumliche Enge und eingeschränkte Bewegungsmöglichkeiten bedeuten. Jan aus der tagesaktuellen Redaktion war bei einer solchen Performance und hat sich mit den Tänzerinnen Eva Amina Kreuter und Krisitna Buketova unterhalten.

title: Adventures in the Terrible Beauty of Resistance With the 'Death to Toll' Campaign
description: In this episode we had the rare opportunity to interview a spokesperson from a direct action group that has targeted Toll Holdings in Australia. The 'Death to Toll' campaign has engaged in a range of sabotage, vandalism and disruptive actions including sledgehammering windows, cutting internet cables, blockading roads and an international port entrance,. They have also slashed lines and cut valves to disable vehicles, covered facilities inside and out with paint and foul liquids, and sabotaged infrastructure such as signal boxes used by Toll. In this discussion we ask them about the development of the anti-zionist movement in Australia after October 7th, 2023. Ask about how the group settled on its target, prepared their campaign, and selected the tactic s they wanted to use in their campaign. As our guest raises the spirit of adventure they see as important to taking meaningful direct action to confront the genocidal war machine, I also ask them what they think about allegations of "adventurism" that can be levied from the left at those who take up such action. Because this campaign is heavily under threat by the state we agreed to some additional security measures in this conversation. The voice you hear is not the actual voice of the person we interviewed. The original interview was transcribed and then converted to audio using a text to voice generator. Just as an editorial note or disclaimer: Amid heightened attacks on various forms of speech, as a platform we are not advocating that people engage in any form of illegal activity. But we do have to understand that the greatest crime that humanity has recognized, the crime of genocide, is still ongoing. There are moral, ethical, and even legal imperatives that people are engaging in order to try to stop that crime from continuing to unfold. This interview is a rare opportunity to hear from those who are taking direct action to halt genocide and war crimes. These actions have been threatened with severe repression and many who take these forms of action do face repression. We see it as a journalistic responsibility to ensure that people hear from those who are willing to take action to stop genocide. It is also very important that people show up and support political prisoners if we are to build a movement that is capable of confronting the machinery of genocide and imperialism. Death to Toll website Other interviews: With Calla Walsh With Islambergerak

title: Pressekonferenz des Landesflüchtlingsrätetreffens mit PRO ASYL (Serie 1513: CX - Corax - Lokales - Mikro)
description: „Asylpolitik unter neuen politischen Bedingungen – aktuelle Entwicklungen, Herausforderungen und Handlungsbedarfe": Unter diesem Titel trafen sich am 18. September 2026 die Landesflüchtlingsräte und PRO ASYL in Halle (Saale) zu einer Pressekonferenz. Im Mittelpunkt standen die aktuellen politischen Entwicklungen in Sachsen-Anhalt und ihre möglichen Auswirkungen auf den Flüchtlingsschutz, Menschenrechte und die Arbeit der Zivilgesellschaft. Die Beteiligten sprachen unter anderem über die zunehmende politische Infragestellung von Menschenrechten und rechtsstaatlichen Prinzipien, die Verschärfung des europäischen Asylsystems und die Situation von Geflüchteten in Sachsen-Anhalt. Ein weiteres Thema war die Forderung nach einer freieren Wahl des Wohnorts für Menschen im Asylverfahren, mit Duldung oder mit Wohnsitzauflage. Die Landesflüchtlingsräte und PRO ASYL betonten die Bedeutung solidarischer Netzwerke und einer engagierten Zivilgesellschaft. Sie kündigten an, auch unter schwieriger werdenden politischen Bedingungen weiter Öffentlichkeit herzustellen, Geflüchtete zu unterstützen und sich gegen Entrechtung einzusetzen.

title: Esperanto Magazin' (Montag) 28.09.2026
Dr. Leonard Harris: Necro-Being & Plato's Allegory of The Cave - (AoE Ep 11)
description: In this episode of Algorithms of Empire, we speak with Dr. Leonard Harris, one of the most influential figures in contemporary African American philosophy, about necro-being, the limits of ethical theory, and the limits of reason itself.Building on his recent lecture, “Necro-Being and the Limits of Ethical Theory,” delivered at the University of Toronto’s Centre for Ethics as part of the Algorithmic Bias Speaker Series, Harris reflects on his concept of necro-being: an approach to racism that foregrounds its material production of premature death, suffering, deprivation, and damaged possibilities for human life. Our conversation also turns to his forthcoming work on the moral imperative against necro-being and what it would mean to construct an ethical response adequate to forms of domination that cannot be reduced to failures of individual intention, prejudice, or rational deliberation.Our discussion then moves from racism and moral philosophy to artificial intelligence. Harris challenges the confidence traditionally placed in reason as the foundation of moral progress, for us to consider what happens when the limitations of human rationality are reproduced—or radically amplified—in artificial superintelligent systems. If reason has never guaranteed moral conduct among human beings, what grounds do we have for assuming that greater computational intelligence will produce wiser or more ethical agents?We were privileged to have Dr. Harris spend his time in a wide-ranging philosophical conversation about racism, death, moral obligation, artificial intelligence, and whether intelligence—human or artificial—is sufficient for confronting the conditions that make necro-being possible.

title: 20/09/2026 – Radioséance: Sürrealismus & Antifaschismus
description: Ihr hört eine Folge von Itty Minchestas Radioséance mit dem Titel „Sürrealismus & Antifaschismus“. Folgende Beschreibung findet sich auf Ittys Homepage: Ursprünglich im Wesen poetisch, ein linguistisches Experiment, entwickelte sich der Sürrealismus zu einer (internat.) Bewegung, die „eine grundsätzliche und radikale Veränderung der politisch-gesellschaftlichen Verhältnisse anstrebte. Während die Kommunisten das Proletariat in der Strategie der Revolution unterwiesen, versuchten die Surrealisten das emotionelle Klima zu erzeugen, in dem diese Revolution ausbrechen könnte.“ (R.Short, 1966). Sie bestanden auf einer absoluten Freiheit, die den Rest der Gesellschaft anstecken sollte. Freiheit: nicht von Lohnarbeit getaktet, jenseits von Nation, Profit und Ausbeutung (auch der Kolonien). Mit Texten von u.a. W.Benjamin, C.Einstein, A.Césaire, P.Yoyotte, E.Lenk, G.Bataille. Ausserdem Thema: Kritische Paranoia vs.Trump, Kritische Theorie & Marxismus. „Widersprüche aushalten, Gegensätze bestehen lassen, parallel auf unterschiedlichen Bahnen denken.“

title: Political Prisoners and the Black Radical Tradition w/Orisanmi Burton [Adnan Husain Show]
description: This is a cross publication from our sister show, The Adnan Husain Show. The Radical Academy is in session for an early edition, 9amET Fri Sept 4! Orisanmi Burton, a social anthropologist at the CUNY Graduate School and author of the profound study, Tip of the Spear: Black Radicalism, Prison Repression and the Long Attica Revolt, joins Office Hours for a discussion of political prisoners, Black radical resistance movements, internationalism and anti-imperialist solidarity. We might have a chance also to talk about his new project that integrates Black Muslim militants thinkers and activists and think about aspects of the relationsip between the Black Radical tradition and socialism/Marxism. We will certainly have much to discuss about the importance of political prisoners in the imperial core and under settler colonial rule from the US to Palestine. Since the open letter addressed rhetorically in the Guardian to political prisoners in Iran and signed by many leading scholars, activists and even political prisoners, the question of the politics around prisoners and solidarity has come further to the fore. Without belaboring that particular controversy, now is an opportune time to learn about and from the experience of political prisoners and resistance. Join us with your questions and comments! title: Building The Infrastructure of Revolt
description: On today's episode, we speak with an organizer with the Let's Go Network a new and growing project from movement builders who are working to provide infrastructure and training to new and emerging social struggles, especially fights against ICE and AI data centers. From the Let's Go website: Let's Go! is a movement infrastructure and support network founded at the end of 2024. We saw that the national political disaster was pushing many movements into immobility, and multiple political currents into stasis. In order to get out of the national malaise and get going again, we came together around the theme of local struggles, where we saw diverse participants fighting in new and vital ways against top-down, oligarchic projects like data centers, Flock surveillance, and ICE infrastructure. We focus on training and movement infrastructure, supporting these local fights from the bottom up and helping them make global impacts. We think local groups and struggles are where the most interesting things are happening and we want to help those involve connect with each other, skill up, and get the resources they need to win. During our discussion, we cover how Let's Go came into being in the post-Trump 2.0 landscape, the hard and long-form work of building autonomous movement infrastructure, and the approach of Let's Go to bringing together various parts of the expansive social movement ecosystem. We also touch on growing efforts by the state to attack the radical flank of existing social movements and the need to intertwine anti-repression and robust solidarity into our organizing, as well as the need for the growing movement against AI and data centers to push back against attempts by the far-Right to latch onto it. We hope that this interview presents listeners with a fresh approach to how we might all work to build up the existing tapestry of emerging social struggles, at a time when repression is ramping up, while waves of new people are also coming into movement organizing like never before. For more information on Let's Go, check out their website at https://letsgonetwork.org/. Also, Let's Go is set to soon release a brand new anti-Data Center organizing resource and broadsheet, which you can check out here. Be sure to also check out two inspiring initiatives against the deportation machine: the ongoing active blockade against border wall construction in Lochiel, AZ. Check out reports from Unicorn Riot and Living and Fighting. There's also been a week of action against ICE called in Willston, VT in early October. Check out shutdownicevt.org and Shut Down ICE VT.

Gerald Perreira: Pan Africanism vs Revolutionary Pan Africanism
description: Gerald Perreira joins Wise The Dome TV for a wide-ranging discussion on Pan-Africanism, Revolutionary Pan-Africanism, socialism, anti-imperialism, and the rapidly changing global political landscape.We examine the current period of global instability, the rise of multipolarity, BRICS, and the growing competition between major powers for influence across Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, and the Global South. The conversation also explores Africa and the new scramble for resources, political developments in the Sahel, Burkina Faso, and the importance of maintaining a critical revolutionary analysis.Other topics include Palestine and its connection to Pan-Africanism, Gaza and the failures of international institutions, Haiti and foreign intervention, the role of the Caribbean in anti-imperialist struggles, and the growing tensions surrounding Guyana, Venezuela, Essequibo, and oil.We also discuss China's growing role in Africa and the Global South, asking whether institutions such as BRICS can create genuine space for formerly colonized nations or whether new centers of power are emerging within the existing global capitalist system.Topics discussed include Pan-Africanism vs. Revolutionary Pan-Africanism, multipolarity, BRICS, Africa, the Sahel, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Ibrahim Traoré, Palestine, Gaza, Haiti, Guyana, Venezuela, Essequibo, China, socialism, imperialism, and the Global South.

title: Elemental Anarchy: A Discussion on the Elements of Mutual Aid
description: The concept of mutual aid has become popularized in the past two decades as an approach to everything from disaster response to meeting basic needs. Even though the term mutual aid is not unique to anarchists, these projects have become a primary way that anarchists spend their time and intervene in the world. While this is promising, some of the roots of the practice, and some of its insurgent possibilities, have been lost throughout this popularization .We sit down with Casa and Maroon to discuss their new documentary series The Elements of Mutual Aid. We discuss the roots of the practice in communities, the ways that mutual aid can escape simple political orthodoxies, and how it can form the foundation of not only a response to the crises that we are living through, but also a route through which we can build the capacity to fight for something better in the midst of collapse. For more information on the documentary, including information on upcoming showings, go to https://theelementsofmutualaid.com/ The series is available for viewing on PeerTube at https://kolektiva.media/c/elementsofmutualaid/videos

description: In this mid-week special, you may have noticed a change in our introduction, that we're listing TFSR.Media as our website (a work in progress, currently pointed at our blog, soon to be pointed at our new web host). description: Breht sits down with philosopher Colin Bodayle for a wide-ranging exploration of Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit , one of the most influential and notoriously difficult works in modern philosophy. title: Myth: Iran Is An Evil Imperialist Regime (W/ Bikrum Gill)
description: In this episode, we bring back political science professor Dr. Bikrum Gil to discuss the myth that Iran is an evil imperialist regime. The analysis goes beyond loving or hating Iran; instead, we ground the conversation in a material approach to understanding what constitutes an imperialist nation and where Iran fits within it. We also explore a recent open letter published in the Guardian titled 'To Iran's political prisoners, trapped 'between two blades of a scissors'. It was signed by several prominent academics and activists, including Angela Davis, Robyn Kelley, and Keeanga-Yamahtta Taylor, among others. It also had political prisoner Mumia Abu-Jamal, but there is deep speculation whether he was aware his name would be used. The letter conflates the imperialist powers of the United States and Israel. Dr. Gill explains how this faulty logic is bigger than one letter but a consequence of Western knowledge production that fails for meet the moment. This leads to the broader discussion on what forms of knowledge help meet the moment, how we need to expand beyond our current canon, and what the resistance teaches us. To Iran's political prisoners, trapped 'between two blades of a scissors' https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/ng-interactive/2026/aug/20/iran-political-prisoners Myth: "I Stand With the Iranian People…BUT" w/ Bikrum Gill https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hZB39oUID1M&t=2719s Patreon https://www.patreon.com/c/blackmyths

title: Mohamed Khougali on the Sudanese Revolution, Civil War, Racial Regimes, & Socially Reproductive Labor
description: In this episode we will speak with Mohamed Khougali about his recently published book Politically Unconscious: The Psychic Aftermath of the Sudanese Revolution, which is out now from our friends at Iskra Books (you can download a free pdf copy). This is an audio version of a video podcast. If you want to watch the video it's available here . Mohamed shares personal insights from his participation with the Neighborhood Resistance Committees during the Sudanese Revolution, he provides a historical backdrop to the Sudanese Civil War, and other moments in which Sudan has become legible to the western audiences, usually only as a site of upheaval or atrocity. It is a powerful conversation that touches on questions of political power, mass revolt, psychotherapy, racial regimes, cooptation, and revolutionary subjectivities. [CONTENT WARNING: The discussion does include discussions of traumatic events and s*xual assault. We do not delve into details or dwell on these stories, but they are used in the context of discussing Khougali's psychotherapeutic practice and events during the revolution] To support our work, gain access to our discord and study groups, please become a patron at https://www.patreon.com/millennialsarekillingcapitalism Mohamed Khougali is a Sudanese socialist writer and psychological practitioner based in Germany, where he continues to organise and serves as president of Black Radicals. His work engages questions of liberation and collective struggle through the combined lenses of the Black radical tradition and psychological theory. Drawing on both intellectual and organisational practice, his research explores the relationship between race, class, colonialism, and subjectivity, with a particular focus on the psychological dimensions of political life and anti-colonial resistance. Check out Mohamed's work with Black Radicals on IG. And if you are interested in his psychotherapeutic practice .

title: Was tun, wenn die Rechte regiert? Lehren aus Israel
description: Gerade richten sich alle Augen auf die Landtagswahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Dort könnte der AfD in wenigen Wochen der Sprung in die Landesregierung gelingen - mit schwer abschätzbaren Konsequenzen für die kritische Zivilgesellschaft und staatliche Behörden, aber vor allem für alle, die nicht in das Weltbild der AfD passen. Doch statt wie das Kaninchen vor der Schlange zu sitzen, wollen wir bei "Was tun?" über die Wahlen hinaus denken. Denn aktuell kippt die Stimmung im ganzen Land immer weiter nach rechts - und so scheint es eine Frage der Zeit zu sein, bis Rechtsextreme mindestens in Bundesländern an die Regierung kommen. Umso wichtiger, sich jetzt schon zu fragen, wie es dann für alle, die für eine solidarische Gesellschaft kämpfen, weiter geht. In der Miniserie "Was tun, wenn Rechte regieren?" sprechen Inken und Valentin mit Aktivist:innen aus Polen, Israel und Brasilien. Sie alle haben Erfahrungen mit rechten Regierungen - und sind sie im Fall von Polen und Brasilien auch wieder losgeworden. Inken und Valentin fragen nach: Wie müssen wir uns Aktivismus unter den neuen Rahmenbedingungen vorstellen? Welche Strategien wirken noch, wenn Rechte unsere Bewegungen zum Feindbild erklären? Und: Wie wird man rechte Regierungen wieder los? In Folge 2 spricht Inken mit Raluca Ganea aus Israel. Dort regiert Benjamin Nathanjahu seit 2022 in einer Koalition mit religiösen Hardlinern und rassistischen Siedlern. Parallel zu den Kriegsverbrechen in Gaza und der Westbank läuft der rechte Staatsumbau in Israel selbst in Hochgeschwindigkeit: politische Rechte palästinensischer Bürger:innen werden immer weiter beschnitten, es gibt Vorstöße, eine Segregation zwischen Männern und Frauen zu etablieren und die demokratische Zivilgesellschaft wird zunehmend eingeschränkt. Raluca ist Gründerin von Zazim, einer Organisation, die in den letzten Jahren zu einer der lautesten Stimmen für ein progressives Israel geworden ist. Gemeinsam mit ihren Kolleg:innen kämpft sie bei Zazim für Solidarität und Demokratie. Inken und Raluca diskutieren darüber, welche Gemeinsamkeiten es zwischen der israelischen Rechten und der AfD gibt, Inken fragt nach, was sich hinter dem Schlagwort der "Re-Humanization" verbirgt und welche drei "Lessons Learned" Raluca für Aktivist:innen in Deutschland parat hat. Zum Schluss diskutieren Valentin und Inken, was wir aus dem Aktivismus in Israel für den Kampf gegen die AfD lernen können. Jetzt reinhören!

title: 23/08/2026 – Bomben, Streiks und Freie Liebe: Anarchismus im „Goldenen Zeitalter“ der USA (Ein Vortrag von Antje Schrupp auf der myzelium 2026)
description: Ein Vortrag von Antje Schrupp auf der myzelium 2026 – https://myzelium-tagung.de Die Jahre zwischen 1870 und 1920 gelten als „goldenes“, oder wie Mark Twain es nannte, „vergoldetes“ Zeitalter der USA. Diese Zeit ist geprägt von rasanter Industrialisierung, Masseneinwanderung, Rassismus und einer Neuverhandlung von Geschlechterverhältnissen. „Anarchismus“ wurde in diesen Jahren zu einem zentralen Schlagwort für gesellschaftliche Debatten, die eine theoretische und praktische Alternative suchten zur bürgerlichen Frauenrechtsbewegung einerseits und den von Marxismus und Sozialdemokratie beeinflussten Arbeiterbewegungen andererseits. In meinem Vortrag skizziere ich die politischen und sozialen Rahmenbedingungen, stelle die maßgeblichen Akteur*innen vor und zeige, wie sich bestimmte inhaltliche Positionen zwischen bürgerlichen Frauenrechtlerinnen und in einem intersektionalen Verständnis miteinander verbanden. Dabei geht es auch darum zu zeigen, dass diese Ereignisse nicht einfach nur von historischer Bedeutung sind, zumal Donald Trump explizit für eine Rückkehr in dieses „Goldene Zeitalter“ wirbt. Dr.Antje Schrupp ist Politikwissenschaftlerin und Journalistin.

title: The Case of the Spokane 3 + Ontological Exhaustion
description: This episode features two segments. title: Producers of Surplus Laborers, Never Citizens: Black Women's Reproduction and Capitalist Empire With T.D. Harper-Shipman
description: In this wide-ranging conversation, Takiyah (T.D.) Harper-Shipman joins us to discuss her new book Unruly Fertility: Race, Development, and Decolonial Reproductive Politics (Stanford University Press, 2026). The discussion traces how modern states—from North Carolina to Senegal—have historically sutured Black women's fertility to the shifting demands of capitalist accumulation, deploying reproductive health policies not as benevolent care but as instruments of crisis management and labor control. Harper-Shipman unpacks the colonial origins of "womanhood" itself as a racialized labor category constructed during European enclosures, one that has always excluded Black women from its aspirational promises of citizenship, consumption, and reproductive autonomy. Drawing on Federici, Mies, Spillers, and Angela Davis, she argues that Black women enter the modern political economy as producers of workers—never citizens—and that contemporary feminist movements risk replicating white womanhood's assumptions when they abandon class analysis or ignore the chains of production behind their demands. The conversation also examines the recent closure of USAID, an institution Takiyah describes as fundamentally about the preservation of white life and the extension of U.S. empire. Rather than mourn its end, she urges us to seize this rupture and continue dismantling the colonial infrastructure of reproductive governance it represented. The conversation closes with a powerful critique of the epistemic violence embedded in global family planning campaigns—how metrics like "unmet need" were designed to serve supplier interests, not Black women's desires, and how Black women's embodied knowledge about contraceptive side effects is systematically dismissed as myth while dangerous technologies banned in the Global North are actively promoted across Africa. Throughout, we explore the Americanization of Black political identity from World War II through 9/11 to Obama's presidency, tracing how Black people have been conscripted into U.S. imperial projects through strategic moments of violence and national belonging. This is Part 1 of a two-part conversation; additional questions will be addressed in an August follow-up. T.D. Harper-Shipman is an Associate Professor and Chair of Africana Studies at Davidson College in North Carolina. She teaches courses and publishes on political economy and its intersection with race and gender in Africa. She has published in p Antipode, Oxford Academic, Third World Quarterly, and International Studies Review, among other places. She is an academic editor at Third World Quarterly and forum editor with the Miami Institute of Social Sciences. Her first book, Rethinking Ownership of Development in Africa was published with Routledge Press in 2019. She has also published in public-facing forums including Africa is a Country and the Global African Worker. title: Socialism and Man in Cuba: Che Guevara and the Revolution of Consciousness
description: Breht reads, reflects upon, and elaborates on Che Guevara's famous essay "Socialism and Man in Cuba" wherein Che argues that socialism cannot be reduced to changing property relations or economic structures; it must also produce a new kind of human being , less alienated, less governed by private self-interest, and more conscious of themselves as a social being. His central claim is that material transformation and the transformation of consciousness have to develop together, through education, collective struggle, moral incentives, self-discipline, and revolutionary practice. ---------------------------------------------------- Learn more here: https://revleftradio.com/ Check out Unlearning Capitalism for more political educational resources

title: Was tun, wenn die Rechte regiert? Lehren aus Polen
description: Gerade richten sich alle Augen auf die Landtagswahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. Dort könnte der AfD in wenigen Wochen der Sprung in die Landesregierung gelingen - mit schwer abschätzbaren Konsequenzen für die kritische Zivilgesellschaft und staatliche Behörden, aber vor allem für alle, die nicht in das Weltbild der AfD passen. Doch statt wie das Kaninchen vor der Schlange zu sitzen, wollen wir bei "Was tun?" über die Wahlen hinaus denken. Denn aktuell kippt die Stimmung im ganzen Land immer weiter nach rechts - und so scheint es eine Frage der Zeit zu sein, bis Rechtsextreme mindestens in Bundesländern an die Regierung kommen. Umso wichtiger, sich jetzt schon zu fragen, wie es dann für alle, die für eine solidarische Gesellschaft kämpfen, weiter geht. In der Miniserie "Was tun, wenn Rechte regieren?" sprechen Inken und Valentin mit Aktivist:innen aus Polen, Israel und Brasilien. Sie alle haben Erfahrungen mit rechten Regierungen - und sind sie im Fall von Polen und Brasilien auch wieder losgeworden. Inken und Valentin fragen nach: Wie müssen wir uns Aktivismus unter den neuen Rahmenbedingungen vorstellen? Welche Strategien wirken noch, wenn Rechte unsere Bewegungen zum Feindbild erklären? Und: Wie wird man rechte Regierungen wieder los? In Folge 1 der Miniserie "Was tun, wenn Rechte regieren?" interviewt Valentin die polnische Aktivistin Dominika Lasota. Dominika kämpfte jahrelang gegen die rechte Regierungspolitik der "Law & Justice" Partei PiS an. Sie war Teil einer Kampagne, die es sich im entscheidenden Wahlkampf zum Ziel gemacht hatte, junge Frauen zur Wahl zu mobilisieren. Doch auch, wenn die Kampagne ein Erfolg war und "Law and Justice" nach acht Jahren an der Macht abgewählt wurde, blickt Dominika mittlerweile kritisch auf ihre Bemühungen, Donald Tusk und seine Mitte-Links-Koalition ins Amt zu hieven. Im Interview spricht sie sich dafür aus, gerade im Kampf gegen Rechts das Verhältnis sozialer Bewegungen zu Parteien zu überdenken - was das bedeutet, hört ihr in der Folge!

Cheikh Bilal: The Sufi Science Of Al Fatihah
description: In this interview, we sit down with Cheikh Bilal to explore the Sufi science and deeper spiritual meaning of Surah Al-Fatihah. We discuss why Al-Fatiha is known as Umm al-Kitab, the significance of its seven verses, its central role in the prayer, and the spiritual dimensions of its words and numbers. Cheikh Bilal also shares insights into the teachings of Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba concerning the recitation of Al-Fatiha and Al-Ikhlas, including their significance in nighttime devotion and spiritual practice. This conversation offers a deeper look at Al-Fatiha as more than a recitation, but as a path toward remembrance, understanding, and a closer relationship with Allah.

title: ABANDON NOBODY: Organizing in Lebanon, Mutual Aid & Survival Under Attack
description: In this episode of The Dugout , we speak with Lebanese anarchists about organizing and surviving through war, occupation, sectarianism, displacement, and economic crisis. We discuss what brought them to anarchism, how they understand Lebanon’s history, and why the experiences of South Lebanon and Beirut can look so different. We talk about the realities of Israel’s attacks, the conditions facing migrant and kafala workers, and the everyday needs people are confronting as communities are displaced and homes are destroyed. At the center of the conversation is a simple principle: abandon nobody. What does solidarity look like when people are already overwhelmed? How do you provide relief without becoming another NGO? And how can anarchists build relationships, share skills, and meet people’s needs without taking control away from the communities they are trying to support? title: #alea - Marx und die Maschine. Eine Einführung
description: Mitschnitt des Vortrags vom 28.07.2026 im Index in Leipzig. Dass künstliche Intelligenz jeden Lebensbereich verändern wird, ist im gegenwärtigen Diskurs eine abgemachte Sache. Im Besonderen soll das auch für die Sphäre der Arbeit gelten. Antizipiert wird eine Welt, in der der Mensch für die Produktion (fast) vollkommen entbehrlich ist. Es sind die Fähigkeiten dieser besonderen Technik selbst, die dieses Versprechen einlösen sollen. Was dabei nicht betrachtet wird, ist wie sich unter den Bedingungen kapitalistischer Produktion eine neue Technik als allgemeine Produktionsweise durchsetzt. Was heute der künstlichen Intelligenz an Potenzial zugeschrieben wird, ist in der Vergangheit schon anderen technischen Entwicklungen zugeschrieben worden: der Digitalisierung, davor der Automation und schließlich auch schon der Maschine. Marx hat in seinem Werk die auch heute noch grundlegende Analyse der kapitalistischen Produktion geliefert. In ihr betrachtet er auch die in seiner Zeit fortgeschrittenste Technik: die Maschine. Im Vortrag wollen wir nachvollziehen, wie Marx die Durchsetzung der maschinenmäßigen Produktion, jenseits einer rein technischen Beschreibung, historisch und politökonomisch analysiert hat. Dafür wollen wir uns das Kapitel “Maschinerie und große Industrie” aus dem ersten Band des Kapitals anschauen und in die dort gemachten Überlegungen einführen. Wir wollen damit auch einen Einstieg für alle ermöglichen, die sich nicht ohnehin schon in den Kategorien von Marx Kritik der politischen Ökonomie auskennen. Wir möchten mit euch überlegen und diskutieren, welche Aspekte auf KI angewendet werden können, was unbeantwortet bleibt und welche Anforderungen an eine kritische Analyse der KI zu stellen wären. Der Vortrag wurde von zwei Mitgliedern der Leipziger Gruppe alea gehalten und fand statt im Rahmen der Veranstaltungsreihe "Künstliche Intelligenz". Weitere Infos zur Veranstaltungsreihe: https://www.alea-le.org/uncategorized/veranstaltungsreihe-kunstliche-intelligenz/

#alea - Surplus ex machina. KI und die Krise des Akkumulationsregimes
description: Mitschnitt des Vortrags vom 14.07.2026 in der Meuterei in Leipzig. Ökonomische Polykrisen erschüttern in immer kürzeren Abständen die globale Ökonomie. Der Zusammenbruch von Ökosystemen und die Klimakrise werden inzwischen nahezu als unvermeidbare Konstante akzeptiert und fungieren als Grundrauschen dieser Polykrise. Dieses Grundrauschen wird durch geopolitische Konflikte, Kriege, Protektionismus und Unsicherheiten bei globalen Lieferketten ergänzt und hat erhebliche Auswirkungen auf ökonomische Entwicklungen und Akteur*innen. Die Kosten für die Bereitstellung von Produkten steigen, während die Nachfrage teilweise sinkt. Diese Entwicklung trifft bisher vor allem klassische Industriebetriebe, werden von dort aber wie Schockwellen weitergegeben. Diese Entwicklungen bleiben auch für politische Systeme in Europa nicht folgenlos. Spätestens seit der Covid-Pandemie sind die politischen Funktionseliten dazu übergegangen Krisen dauerhaft zu verwalten anstatt gesellschaftliche Transformation zu gestalten. Dabei werden drei Mantras beschworen: Bürokratieabbau, Innovationsfähigkeit und Technologieoffenheit. Der Einsatz von künstlicher Intelligenz (kurz: AI/KI) gilt als Heilsbringer. Dabei wird der Begriff zusehends zu einer Projektionsfläche. Riesige Erwartungen und mindestens genauso viel Geld werden in die Bereitstellung von neuen Modellen und die dafür notwendigen Ressourcen gesteckt. Dass der Einsatz von KI gesellschaftliche Strukturen maßgeblich verändern wird, scheint unbestritten. Darüber scheinen sich die Mächte des alten Europas, der Papst, vermutlich einige französische Radikale und sicherlich deutsche Polizist*innen einig zu sein. Der Vortrag führt zunächst zentrale Grundbegriffe aus den Bereichen Datenwertschöpfung, Analytics und KI ein und vermittelt ein grundlegendes Verständnis der Funktionsweise und Anwendungsfelder von KI-Systemen. Anschließend sollen anhand einiger Fallbeispiele die Kapitalströme rund um KI-Unternehmen und die zugrundeliegenden Erwartungen analysiert werden, um die Frage zu klären, welcher ökonomische Mehrwert durch KI-Technologien erreicht werden soll. Abschließend soll diskutiert werden, welche gesellschaftlichen Verwerfungen sich rund um das Themenfeld KI auftun und welche Kämpfe es zu führen gilt. Zum Referenten: Manuel hat Volkswirtschaftslehre, Informatik und Sozialwissenschaften studiert und lebt in Nürnberg. Er arbeitet als Softwarearchitekt und Projektleiter bei einer IT-Beratung und entwickelt dort Dateninfrastrukturen und -plattformen. Er beschäftigt sich mit der Frage, welche Ansätze und Technologien aus der Informatik für sozial-ökologische Transformation und postkapitalistisches Wirtschaften geeignet sind. Der Vortrag fand statt im Rahmen der Veranstaltungsreihe "Künstliche Intelligenz", ausgerichtet von der Leipziger Gruppe alea. Weitere Infos zur Veranstaltungsreihe: https://www.alea-le.org/uncategorized/veranstaltungsreihe-kunstliche-intelligenz/

title: Algorithms of Empire (Episode 10); Special Guest: Dr. Ashique KhudaBukhsh
description: In this episode of Algorithms of Empire, we speak with Dr. Ashique KhudaBukhsh about his team's startling discovery: advanced AI models can be persuaded to accept falsehoods as truth through nothing more than conversational pressure. What began as a casual observation—ChatGPT confidently inventing a non-existent Hitler reference in Good Will Hunting—turned into a systematic study of five leading models across 2,000 movies and novels. Dr. KhudaBukhsh and his team found that soft nudges like "I'm pretty sure…" or "I remember it this way…" could make AI systems abandon facts they initially verified, with Claude emerging as the most resistant and Gemini and DeepSeek the most easily swayed. Dr. KhudaBukhsh draws a crucial distinction between hallucination (fabricating information outright) and sycophancy (capitulating to a user's false premise), arguing these are two distinct vulnerabilities requiring different fixes—a nuance that traditional AI evaluations routinely miss.The stakes extend far beyond movie trivia. Dr. KhudaBukhsh walks us through how this "nudge" dynamic could play out in high-stakes domains like healthcare, law, and public policy, where an AI's willingness to validate a user's incorrect assumption could have serious real-world consequences. The conversation also grapples with deeper questions of collective memory, accountability, and design incentives: if AI systems are trained to prioritize user satisfaction over factual consistency, then their "truth" is not anchored to reality but malleable to whoever speaks with the most confidence. This makes LLMs not neutral arbiters of information but (in many potential cases) active participants in the spread of misinformation—and it forces us to ask whether AI-human alignment as currently conceived is less about anchoring AI to objective truth and more about designing it to flatter whichever human happens to be asking the questions.Dr. KudaBukhsh's research we discussed in this episode can be found here: https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-lon.. .

description: Seit 2001 existiert in Berlin-Hellersdorf das AJZ Kita, samt Veranstaltungslocation La Casa. Kneipe, Sportraum, Werkstätten und auch Wohnraum finden sich dort. title: LIGNA Das Wunder von Hamburg [POSITION. Forum aus Mai 2026]
description: Das Radio Ballett lädt die TeilnehmerInnen ein, in ehemals öffentlichen, inzwischen privatisierten und kontrollierten Orten wie Hauptbahnhöfen oder Shopping Malls, einer Choreographie von verbotenen und ausgeschlossenen Gesten zu folgen. Das Publikum wird dabei zu einem Kollektiv von ProduzentInnen. Es entsteht eine Assoziation, die unvorhersehbare, unkontrollierbare Effekte hervorbringt, welche die Ordnung des Raumes herausfordern. Ortsspezifische Arbeiten eröffnen dem Publikum die Möglichkeit, in öffentliche Räume zu intervenieren, oder diese, wie zuletzt in der Bustour über René Benkos Hamburger Ruinen neu zu sehen (Das Wunder von Hamburg). In vielen von LIGNAs Arbeiten geht es um vergessene historische Momente – seien es die weitflächig abgerissenen Gängeviertel (Schafft ein, zwei, viele Gänge!), umstrittene Monumente der Vergangenheit wie das Haus des Kommunismus in Buzludzha (Nonument) oder das erste bundesdeutsche Happening von Wolf Vostell in den Ruinen Kölns (Cityrama 3) – und die Frage, welche zukünftige Gestalten der urbane Raum annehmen könnte. POSITION. Ausstellung und Forum ist eine Veranstaltungsreihe des Berufsverbands bildender Künstler*innen Hamburg. LIGNA war mit diesem Vortrag Gast am 17. Mai. | https://www.bbk-hamburg.de | https://www.ligna.org/ | redaktion3@fsk-hh.org

title: Voci dal corteo No Ponte
description: Voci dalla manifestazione No ponte Durata 32m 45s Oltre 10.000 persone in piazza a Messina contro il ponte e per la chiusura della Stretto di Messina s.p.a. Delegazioni da ogni parte d'Italia, ma soprattutto da Sicilia è Calabria, hanno manifestato per pretendere la chiusura della società che dal 1981 ha drenato oltre un miliardo di euro di fondi pubblici senza nemmeno posare una pietra. Grande pluralità all'interno del corteo, che storicamente non si è mai limitato a dire semplicemente "no" al ponte ma ha sempre restituito un ampio ecosistema di comitati che si battono contro il sistema estrattivo e di sfruttamento del territorio. Dissesto idrogeologico, mancanza di servizi, emergenza sanitaria e abitativa, carenza di infrastrutture sono solo alcuni dei temi portati all'attenzione dell'opinione pubblica come possibili alternative di impiego degli oltre 13 miliardi di fondi stanziati per il ponte. Intanto, sul piano tecnico, il Ponte sullo Stretto ha ottenuto il via libera del Consiglio superiore dei lavori pubblici. Non è però la parola fine: si passa ora al progetto esecutivo, con verifiche aggiuntive richieste su altezza dell'opera, faglie sismiche e rischio terremoti. Il governo spinge, avendo dichiarato l'opera di "rilevante interesse pubblico" per accelerare le autorizzazioni. Ma i passaggi decisivi restano altri due: il Cipess e, soprattutto, la Corte dei Conti, che un anno fa aveva già bocciato il progetto. Restano diverse incognite legali: un esposto della Cgil sui fondi europei dirottati dalla Sicilia al Ponte, le proteste di alcuni Comuni coinvolti e due indagini penali aperte a Roma e Caltanissetta. Salvini vorrebbe posare la prima pietra entro le elezioni, l'ad della Stretto di Messina s.p.a. Ciucci vorrebbe terminare l'opera entro il 2033. Si preannuncia una stagione di mobilitazione, la radio seguirà da vicino le vicende dello Stretto e non solo.

title: The New Red Scare: Trump's War on the American Left
description: In this episode, Alyson and Breht examine the Trump administration's emerging campaign against what it calls "far-left terrorism." We begin with NSPM-7, the presidential directive encouraging federal agencies to investigate not only alleged political violence, but the organizations, funders, media networks, and ideological communities surrounding it. We then look at two distinct examples of this framework in practice: the sweeping Prairieland prosecutions in Texas, where defendants received extraordinarily severe terrorism-related sentences, and the separate crackdown in Minnesota following anti-ICE mobilizations and political unrest. From there, we analyze Marco Rubio and Stephen Miller's international counterterrorism summit, the effort to redirect the machinery of the War on Terror toward the anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist left, and the State Department's Cuba document, which portrays socialism, anti-imperialism, Palestine solidarity, and antifascism as parts of a foreign-influenced revolutionary network. Finally, we ask whether the United States has entered a new Red Scare, what may come next, and how left-wing individuals, media outlets, and organizations can protect themselves without abandoning their political work. Lettere dal carcere di Ahmad Salem
description: Lettura lettere di Ahmad Salem Durata 10m 12s Lettura delle lettere dal carcere del palestinese Ahmad Salem Ahmad Salem, 24enne palestinese cresciuto in uno dei più grandi campi profughi palestinesi, Al-Baddawi, ha lasciato il paese per cercare un futuro. Dopo un primo passaggio in alcune città europee, è arrivato in Italia e si è presentato alla commissione territoriale di Campobasso per richiedere la protezione internazionale. In quell'occasione, durante la procedura di identificazione, mentre mostrava alcune fotografie dei propri documenti, il suo telefono è stato ispezionato. Al suo interno sono stati trovati un video pubblicato su TikTok, in cui denunciava il silenzio della comunità internazionale e dei Paesi arabi di fronte alla guerra a Gaza, alcune conversazioni private e video delle Brigate Al-Qassam, già disponibili online e rilanciati anche da diversi media italiani e non. Questi contenuti sono stati però motivo di arresto e, successivamente, della condanna a 4 anni di carcere per istigazione a delinquere e auto-addestramento con finalità di terrorismo, in applicazione delle nuove norme (dl sicurezza 2025) sul cosiddetto "terrorismo della parola". Questa storia sembra voler equiparare il sostegno alla causa palestinese come terrorismo e ampliare con approccio repressivo e autoritario l'uso del diritto penale vorso chi resiste e dissente. Il solo possesso di materiale digitale è motivo oggi di arresto e detenzione. Inoltre, questa storia racconta anche la persecuzione delle istituzioni italiane verso le persone migranti trattate come minacce. Il desiderio di avere una vita vivibile viene trasformato in un inferno, quali sono le carceri italiane. Questa sentenza non è un caso isolato, ma il riflesso di una strategia repressiva che colpisce chiunque denunci il genocidio e l'occupazione della Palestina. title: Meeting mass migration with 'Welcome Tables' (not walls) with Josh Fox
description: The world as we knew it is no more. It sounds dark, trite, and reductive, but there's a truth in there that can't be denied. All signs point to the global climate changing faster than most scientists predicted . In the news, we see stories about extreme heat waves causing tens of thousands of deaths, ongoing droughts impacting the global food supply, and the accelerated loss of polar ice caps. At the same time, for many of us, the reliability of the seasons we once had is no more. In my neck of the woods in Northern California, it was 80 degrees in February, and then it was so cold at the beginning of July that we had to fire up the woodstove! And while the changing weather may be a mild inconvenience for some of us, it can be catastrophic for others, especially for those in the global south who have contributed the least to the climate emergency. Many areas along the equator and in the southern hemisphere will become increasingly uninhabitable over the next 50 years, with one prominent study projecting that as many as three billion people will be forced to migrate to the Northern Hemisphere. That's roughly a third of the global population! Even if it's only the low side of that estimate, the migration of a billion people would completely transform every nation on the planet. For the 100th episode of The Response Podcast , we interviewed Academy Award-nominated and Emmy-winning documentary filmmaker Josh Fox about the climate crisis, human migration, and how to welcome those coming rather than meet them with walls and brutal criminalization. Josh's new film, The Welcome Table , is now available to watch on HBO Max. About the guest Josh is an independent filmmaker and founder and artistic director of International WOW Company . His films include AWAKE. A Dream From Standing Rock , How To Let Go Of The World And Love All The Things Climate Can't Change , and the award-winning Gasland and Gasland 2 . Nirule Salaam: Yale, Slavery, & New Haven Connecticut
description: Nirule Salaam: Yale, Slavery, & New Haven ConnecticutNirule Salaam is a New Haven community historian whose family has been in the city for generations. His book, Y.A.L.E: Black Power vs Biopower, traces Yale University's role in American racial governance from 1638 to today. He wrote it without institutional backing—no grants, no fellowships, no permission from any entity it names. This is not an apology tour. It's a prosecution. And it demands restitution, not acknowledgment.We talk about Neagar Anthony, the captive held in 1638 before Yale existed; Ezra Stiles, Yale's seventh president, who bought a ten-year-old boy, renamed him "Newport," and held him for 21 years; the 700-to-4 vote against a Black college in New Haven in 1831; and the contemporary frame of Fred James, Sarah Burns, and Ron DeSantis—all in the same city at the same time. Salaam also presents "the invoice": a specific accounting of what Yale extracted, what it destroyed, and what it still owes.The book is history for the Hip Hop generation. The community names the wound before the institution admits it exists. This interview lets Salaam name names.Link to book: https://www.nadirsalaam.com/copy-of-host-bio

title: Toward Indigenous Self-Determination: Fourth World Theory and Indigenous Marxism
description: In this episode, Breht speaks with his guests Pavin and Jennifer Marley from Total Sovereignty Working Group about George Manuel's Fourth World theory and the Indigenous Marxist traditions of Howard Adams and Lee Maracle. Together, they examine the conflict between land as capitalist property and land as a living relationship; the formation of colonial-racial capitalism; and the limitations of state-recognized self-government, "Red capitalism," and settler socialism. They also explore the tension between Indigenous self-determination as a transitional stage toward universal socialism and as the permanent reconstruction of Indigenous nationhood, territorial authority, and collective responsibility, as well as Maracle's insistence that decolonization must include feminism, rematriation, and the restoration of Indigenous women's governing power. Ultimately, the conversation asks what it would mean to abolish capitalism and settler colonialism together—and to create forms of collective life grounded in reciprocity, land, care, and genuine self-determination. Total Sovereignty Working Group is a Native focus group dedicated to building a strategy for winning back our land and caring for our nations. title: Myth: Good Socialist, Bad Communist (w/ Dr. Charisse Burden-Stelly)
description: In this episode, we explore the false dichotomy between the "Good Socialist" and the "Bad Communist." This is the idea that one can separate oneself from anti-communism by dissing communism. However, with the State Department's release of Cuba: The Capital of the 21st Century, targeting anything progressive as "domestic terrorism, it becomes clearer that everyone marginally left is a target. Historically, Black people, whether left-wing or not, are vulnerable to these types of red scares, and thus should be prepared. To help us discuss these dilemmas, we bring on a friend of the show, Dr. Charise Burden-Stelly. She is an Associate Professor of African American Studies at Wayne State University and the author of the book Black Scare / Red Scare: Theorizing Capitalist Racism in the United States. We discuss anti-communism, what it is, the contradictions it creates, and ways to remain principled in combating it. We also look at the way Anti-communism is weaponized to target Black radical movements. This is part 1 of 2. For Patreon subscribers who want to listen to both parts, part 2 is available. If you're not a subscriber, please sign up. https://www.patreon.com/c/blackmyths Dr. CBS https://www.charisseburdenstelly.com/ Myth: Communism Made Me Do It https://www.youtube.com/live/ZXuC-rPwYZ8?is=3eiIf9R9MGp34P30 Myth: Communism Made Me Do It Pt. 2 https://www.youtube.com/live/V4OSrY-tFvY?is=KkWz1ct4YzATtlsv Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism https://www.state.gov/cuba-the-capital-of-21st-century-communism NATIONAL SECURITY PRESIDENTIAL MEMORANDUM/NSPM-7 https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/countering-domestic-terrorism-and-organized-political-violence/

title: Cal & Isaac of The Minnesota 15 on ICE Watch & The Federal Indictment
description: Guests:Cal & Isaac, two of the Minnesota 15 defendants In this episode of The Dugout, we sit down with Cal and Isaac, two of the fifteen people indicted following Operation Metro Surge, the federal immigration occupation of the Twin Cities. We trace their political histories, from labor organizing and anti-cult work to anti-fascist organizing, and get a firsthand account of the ICE occupation of Minneapolis-St. Paul: the killing of Renee Goode, the general strike of January 23rd, and the federal raids that led to their arrest and indictment. We discuss the specific repression they're facing (including a pre-dawn SWAT raid): months-long surveillance, and federal charges that they argue amount to "thought crimes" and what kind of support actually matters right now. The Unglamorous Labor of Movement Building
description: (Photo by Shwetha Shankar on Unsplash ) Dear friends, July has been one of the most eventful months of the year. I travelled to Southeast Asia to attend a partner-led writing retreat before joining my colleagues in Bangkok to host the 2nd Regional Networking Conference, bringing together platform worker organizations and civil society from across Asia. Now back home in the US, I’m taking time to process the connections, exchanges, and insights from these two gatherings. Having worked in relative isolation for the past two years, this was a rare opportunity to meet and reconnect with peers across Asia. In this piece, reflecting on this whirlwind trip, I share insights from our discussions on why an infrastructure of trust-building is essential to creating sustainable networks. Asian Labor Futures is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Structure and Infrastructure It might sound cliché to say that interpersonal relationships are the foundation of movement-building. Yet mistrust and conflict remain ones of the most common forces tearing collectives apart. Conflict is like an elephant in the room that we rarely address until it is too late. This is where the distinction between structure and infrastructure becomes useful. Organizational structure is the architecture of what we do together. Too often, we build rigid structures that assume smooth sailing, leaving them brittle and prone to snapping when crisis arises. We can, and should, design structures that are explicitly built to handle crisis and tension, such as rotating decision-making bodies and transparent governance rules. However, even the most conflict-responsive structure will fall apart without the infrastructure beneath it. Infrastructure is the underlying system that enables organizations to communicate with and lean on one another. Importantly, movement infrastructure is never just one thing: it spans both the formal and the informal, the tangible and the intangible. The Layers of Movement Infrastructure For me, it was sharing meals with organizers and unwinding after long conference days that created the room for genuine connection. Those casual, late-night chats, when we all finally let our guards down, built a deep understanding of each other's limits, hopes, and fears. It built the kind of trust and safety net that no formal agenda ever could. When crisis hits our groups, a formal mediation protocol will fail if there is no underlying reservoir of trust to animate it. On the contrary, personal goodwill alone quickly dissolves into chaotic infighting if there are no concrete channels or allocated resources to process disagreement safely. To make those informal spaces meaningful, they must be backed by formal commitments: dedicated time and budget lines built directly into conference agendas for debriefing, paired with explicit, pre-agreed guidelines for surfacing grievances without threatening anyone’s standing in the coalition. Interpersonal relationships are the most basic layer of movement infrastructure, yet they are frequently treated as an afterthought. The unglamorous labor of building trust, maintaining friendships, and holding space for difficult conversations is often relegated to leisure time or dependent on professional facilitators. Building Infrastructure That Grows With Conflicts If we accept that disagreement is natural, we must stop viewing conflict as an anomaly or a failure. Too often, organizations handle conflict in one of two counterproductive ways: they sweep it under the rug to preserve surface-level harmony, or they let unaddressed grievances explode, splintering hard-won networks. Building resilient networks requires us to invest in every dimension of solidarity infrastructure including conflict literacy. Just as physical buildings require underground shock absorbers to survive earthquakes, cross-border solidarity require built-in systems to absorb conflict
